key_insight: Flow-dependent LES filter-widths can transmit floating-point perturbations almost without attenuation when they depend on directional mesh metrics, making numerical sensitivity an active modeling issue.
engineering_relevance: For heterogeneous CPU/GPU LES workflows, the paper offers a more robust filter-width formulation that preserves flow dependence while reducing sensitivity to architecture-induced roundoff effects.
method: Analyze how LSQ-based filter-width responds to metric perturbations under fixed resolved kinematics
Add a scalar max–min compression of directional mesh scales plus a bounded velocity-gradient modulation
Compare the original and modified formulations on heterogeneous CPU/GPU runs
evidence_signal: The approach is evaluated on flow past a circular cylinder at Re=3900 and the Taylor–Green vortex at Re=1600, showing near one-to-one metric perturbation transmission in the cylinder case but no comparable macroscopic response on orthogonal Taylor–Green grids.
watch_item: The robustness gain may depend on mesh anisotropy and flow geometry, so the modified operator should be checked carefully before use in strongly directional or transition-sensitive LES cases.
paper_title: On the transmission of floating-point perturbations in flow-dependent filter-width formulations in Large-Eddy Simulation
